tour.overview:
Most visitors to Bora Bora see the island from the lagoon, but the interior has its own treasures: steep ridges with views over the lagoon, old Polynesian marae, and the cannons left by the 5,000 American soldiers who built a supply base here in 1942, during the Second World War. The island's main village, Vaitape, and the long white beach of Matira complete the picture.

This private half-day takes you around and up into the island by 4x4 with a local guide.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 4 hours
• Start and end: your hotel or Vaitape quay
• Type: private 4x4 with local guide and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy; bumpy tracks

WHAT YOU SEE
• The lagoon viewpoints.
• The WWII cannons.
• Marae.
• Vaitape.
• Matira Beach.

WHY THIS WORKS
A private 4x4 reaches viewpoints that cars cannot, and your guide shares the island’s history and legends.

WHO IT SUITS
Families, couples and anyone curious about the island beyond the resorts.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For the lagoon, choose our Bora Bora lagoon tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The tracks are steep and bumpy; not recommended for people with back problems or pregnant women.

days.name: Viewpoints, WWII cannons, marae, Vaitape and Matira Beach
days.description:
What to expect: the island interior and its history, by private 4x4.

Your guide and driver collect you at about 8:30 and drive around the island road to Vaitape, the main village, with its church and craft market. You then climb by 4x4 up steep tracks through the tropical forest to the ridges, where the cannons installed by American troops in 1942 still point out to sea. From the top, the view takes in the whole lagoon, the motus and the luxury overwater bungalows, with Mount Otemanu rising behind you.

On the way down, you visit a marae, a sacred stone platform where ancient Polynesians held ceremonies, and your guide explains their beliefs and the legends of the island. You stop at a workshop where artisans print pareos with leaves and flowers in the sun, and taste tropical fruit such as papaya, pineapple and starfruit. You end at Matira Beach, where you can swim before returning to your hotel.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:30 – Pick-up.
09:00 – Vaitape village.
09:30 – 4x4 to the viewpoints and WWII cannons.
10:30 – Marae.
11:00 – Pareo workshop and fruit.
11:45 – Matira Beach.
12:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Combine it with an afternoon lagoon tour for a full day.
• Bring swimwear for Matira Beach.

INCLUDED: private 4x4 and driver, local guide, pareo workshop, fruit tasting, bottled water, pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: fruit tasting.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Is the 4x4 private?
faq.answer: Yes, a private vehicle with driver and guide.

faq.question: Is it bumpy?
faq.answer: Yes, the tracks to the viewpoints are steep and rough.

faq.question: Can we combine it with the lagoon tour?
faq.answer: Yes, morning 4x4 and afternoon lagoon is a popular combination.

faq.question: Can we climb Mount Otemanu?
faq.answer: No. The summit is unstable and closed; the hike to Mount Pahia is possible with a specialist guide.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes, for children over about 4. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Not really, because of the bumpy tracks. Ask us for a road-only version.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: No, but fruit is. Matira has restaurants by the beach.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: Only the pareo workshop, with no obligation to buy.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Light clothes, a hat, sun cream and swimwear.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: All year. May to October is drier.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is not customary in French Polynesia and is never expected, but a small gesture for excellent service is always appreciated.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
